newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank to tighten payment supervision.
newsitem.headline: China central bank to tighten payment supervision.

text.p: The People's Bank of China, the central bank, will tighten supervision of payments and settlements in commercial banks, spreading the use of commercial bills to reduce risk, state media said on Sunday.
Flawed payments and settlements were one reason for expensive and complicated debt chains among enterprises, the China Daily Business Weekly quoted a bank official as saying.
A growing number of China's enterprises are weighed down by a mountain of debt, much of which cannot be repaid.
The bank would promote the use of commercial bills, the official said. Financial institutions now limit the use of commercial bills, promissory notes, cheques and credit cards by enterprises.

The central bank would also promote a system of "Three Nos", the official said. These are no delivery without payment, no delivery without commercial bills and no delivery if the buyer does not repay outstanding bills.
The coal, electricity, chemical and railway industries adopted this practice last year, helping to speed up capital flow and prevent defaults, the official said.
In 1996, 95 percent of coal industry loans were recalled and some debts in default were paid, he said.
This year, the central bank plans to exercise commercial bill settlement in large and medium enterprises, grain plants and agricultural producers.
The bank would try to develop letters of credit and would issue a regulation on the usage, the official said.
